target.statement: Mean held-out log copula density per subject for the four-family (Clayton/Gumbel/Frank/Gaussian) copula mixture fitted to within-sex standardized 50-m sprint and standing long jump scores of students: 0.1079, i.e. a gain of 0.0050 (SE 0.0011) over a single Gaussian copula (0.1029).
target.table_ref: Table 4, row 'Students: speed, power / Four-family, K = 4'
target.dataset: Jiangxi university student physical fitness tests (8772 students; supporting dataset S1 of Sun et al. 2024a)

compute.basis: No code is released, so the four-family marginal Metropolis sampler (Algorithm 1), the Gaussian-copula baselines, the stratified train/eval split and the held-out scoring must all be re-implemented; the paper reports ~40-300 s per four-family fit on a laptop CPU, so a handful of chains plus baselines is a few hours of command time, dominated by debugging the re-implementation.

blockers: No code or repository linked anywhere in the paper
Student fitness data are a third-party supporting dataset (Sun et al. 2024a) that must be located and downloaded separately
Exact train/eval split and tie-breaking must be reconstructed from the text; results are sensitive to the random split
MCMC sampler details (adaptation, independence proposals, chain lengths) only partly specified
title: Bayesian heterogeneous copula mixtures with nonparametric margins: consistency, identifiability and tail asymmetry in physical fitness data
